clue.text: It's incumbent upon the very small to be fashionable

parts.note: a duty incumbent upon you is up to you
minute (my-NEWT) means tiny

explanation.surface: Someone declares that keeping in style is the duty of tiny folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link word; 'incumbent upon' reads as the phrase UP TO, as in 'it's up to you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are current and in vogue are said to be bang up-to-date, the latest thing.

clue.text: Paradoxically, this defines "downs"

parts.note: downs are rolling chalk hills, so the word for high ground with 'up' in it describes places called 'downs' — the paradox

explanation.walkthrough: The South Downs and North Downs are ranges of chalk hills in southern England, despite the name suggesting low ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Downs are elevated grassy hill country, which is exactly higher terrain inland.

clue.text: Punk has to guard against misfortune

definitions.meaning: punk is an old word for rotten wood used as tinder
saying the phrase while tapping wood is a superstition to ward off bad luck

explanation.surface: A punk rocker is obliged to protect against bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed wood used to catch a spark is called punk; the superstitious phrase is uttered to avert a jinx.

clue.text: Cast finished speaking

indicators.note: speaking says the word for finished is to be pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: when you are through, you are finished

explanation.surface: An actor's company finished talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatre company, but it is the past tense of the verb, meaning flung.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a stone is to hurl or toss it; the past tense is the same.

clue.text: 7 nameless children sorted out — about time

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
sorted out signals that the remaining letters of the word are rearranged
nameless tells us to drop the abbreviation for name from the word that follows

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Some unnamed youngsters are organised, with a clock running.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer at 7 down, EERIE, which is the definition. 'nameless' removes N from CHILDREN, leaving CHILDRE; 'sorted out' makes ELDRICH of it; 'about' puts that around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something weird and unearthly that sends a shiver down the spine.

clue.text: Finest fellow moved inside to invade

indicators.note: moved inside says that letter shifts from the front of the word into its interior

explanation.surface: The best man relocated to occupy another territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved inside' shifts the F of FINEST from the front to sit after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests that overrun a place swarm into it, as an army would occupy hostile ground.

clue.text: Ready to fight in the pits?

definitions.meaning: troops ... are equipped and prepared for battle
the pits here are armpits, the hollows beneath the shoulders

explanation.surface: A soldier is primed for combat while down in the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'the pits' suggests trenches or a mine, but it means armpits.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers bearing weapons are mobilised; the hollows below the shoulders are a person's armpits.

clue.text: Strange career I enjoyed, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that the working life they loved was an odd one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird and uncanny, giving an unsettling feeling, is strange.

clue.text: Get hold of a lot of eggs

definitions.meaning: the batch of eggs a bird lays and sits on at one time

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grab plenty of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab firmly is to seize; a hen's sitting of eggs is the same word as a noun.

clue.text: Provided with openings to admit air, museum's finally ventilated

definitions.text: Provided with openings to admit air

parts.note: the Louvre is the famous museum in Paris

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word ventilated

explanation.surface: A Paris gallery has at last been aired, fitted with vents.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatted shutters with angled strips let air through while keeping rain out.

clue.text: In league with ref, deal worked out

indicators.note: worked out says the letters of these two words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A referee is said to be colluding over a fixed deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: States joined in a union under a central government are allied together, confederated.

clue.text: Expertise listened to? Not at all commonly

indicators.note: listened to says the word for expertise is heard rather than written, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: know-how is practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether skill is heeded and answers that it never is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks the answer as dialect or nonstandard speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word for 'in no way at all', used in informal or rustic speech.

clue.text: Unresting, unruly and "rebellious

indicators.note: unruly says the letters of the preceding word run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A restless, disorderly and defiant character is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rising in revolt against authority is a rebel, so as an adjective it means mutinous.

clue.text: This will staunch the flow from second and first in pecking order

parts.note: the top cock is the dominant bird heading a flock's pecking order

explanation.surface: A remedy for bleeding is said to come from the runner-up and the boss of the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve fitted in a water pipe is turned to shut off the supply.

clue.text: In haste, bishop produces a name

indicators.note: In says the abbreviation for bishop goes inside the word for haste

parts.note: celerity means swiftness or haste
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A hurried bishop is said to produce a famous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous person is 'a big name', a star.

clue.text: Whinger sees Marx giving nothing away

indicators.note: giving ... away together say a letter is removed from the name
away completes the phrase giving away, meaning take out

parts.note: Groucho was the moustached Marx brother
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A complainer watches Karl's namesake donating nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumbler who is always moaning and complaining is a whinger.

clue.text: Routine rises in annual arrangement that's abnormal

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the rearranged letters
arrangement says the letters of annual are reordered
rises, in a down clue, says the word for routine reads upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: Daily habit climbing within a yearly scheme is thought odd.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' reads the word upwards; 'arrangement' scrambles the yearly word and 'in' puts the reversed routine inside it. 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary to nature and deviating from the norm, as unnatural behaviour is odd.

clue.text: Landlord who used to be a taxman

definitions.meaning: the landlord of a pub or inn runs the bar

definitions.text: who used to be a taxman
definitions.meaning: in ancient Rome the publicani were tax collectors, as in the Bible

explanation.surface: A property owner turns out to have formerly collected revenue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'landlord' is a British pub keeper, not someone who lets houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub keeper holds the licence; in the Gospels the tax gatherers were translated this way.

clue.text: Get boat's propeller to move in shallow water

definitions.meaning: the bladed oar or wheel that drives a boat
to wade about at the edge of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fetch the boat's means of propulsion to get it through the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A short oar drives a canoe; children wade in the shallows with bare feet.

clue.text: Children's writer who makes a slip intentionally?

definitions.meaning: Beatrix ... wrote the Peter Rabbit books
slip is liquid clay, which a ceramics maker makes on purpose

explanation.surface: An author for youngsters is accused of erring deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' looks like a mistake, but it is the potter's watery clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix of that surname wrote famous animal tales; a ceramicist throwing pots prepares clay slip.

clue.text: Travelling slower than some craft, vessel with child in charge

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A slow boat puttering along is captained by a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; the 'some craft' that are faster are supersonic aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving below the speed of sound is slower than supersonic jets fly.

clue.text: Pact was broken — it produces ripples

indicators.note: broken says the letters of these words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An agreement was violated, causing ripples of discontent.
explanation.definitionFit: A light breeze that ruffles calm water is named after a feline's foot.

clue.text: Contemplate unpleasant smell in summer house

parts.note: to gaze is to look at steadily, contemplating
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a nasty odour in a garden building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden pavilion with a view, built for sitting in during warm weather.

clue.text: Short — in general, two and a quarter inches

parts.note: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of the tiny 19th-century circus performer
the nail is an old measure of cloth, two and a quarter inches

explanation.surface: Something brief is described in terms of an old length measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. General Tom Thumb was the famous small entertainer shown by P. T. Barnum.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a brief, concise description, so short.

clue.text: Unexceptional learner attending university in America

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the learner's letter joins on alongside
in says the abbreviation for university goes inside the country

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An ordinary student goes to college in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside USA to make USUA; 'attending' adds L after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and customary, nothing out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Cherished one-time minor, legally speaking

parts.note: a pet is a cherished favourite
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A beloved former child is described in legal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time' looks like 'former', but splits into one (I) and time (T).
explanation.definitionFit: In law the French-derived word means small or lesser, as in petty larceny.

clue.text: Drink for horse

definitions.meaning: a mixed drink of spirits, fruit and spice
the Suffolk ... is a heavy English draught horse

explanation.surface: Something to drink is offered for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of mixed fruity alcohol at a party; the Suffolk breed of carthorse.

clue.text: Learned it in English course, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the assembled letters are only heard, giving a word pronounced the same way

parts.note: IT goes in E (English) and ROUTE (course), giving E-ROUT-IT-E, said 'e-root-ite'

explanation.surface: Someone picked up information in an English class, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' is the adjective (LER-nid), not the past tense of learn.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly person with great knowledge from study is well read.

clue.text: Pious language used by reprobate — it's a trick

parts.note: cant is hypocritical sanctimonious talk
a rip is a dissolute rogue

explanation.surface: A scoundrel mouths sanctimonious words as a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a witch's spell or a mischievous piece of magic, a prank.

clue.text: Be authoritarian and begin to build wealth corruptly

parts.note: to lay down a foundation is to start building

indicators.note: corruptly says the letters of wealth are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone domineering starts amassing riches dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate and insist that others obey rules is to be bossy and dogmatic.
